OVERALL VERDICT
"Well-packaged metadata sits on top of an almost empty page, so the site currently looks more like a placeholder than a usable portfolio."

The page has several technical basics in place: HTTPS, canonical, viewport, Open Graph tags, favicon, and Person schema. But the actual page content is effectively absent: there is no visible body copy, no headings, no links, no projects, and no calls to action. That makes it weak for users, poor for conversion, and critically thin for search despite a solid title and meta description.

31
SCORE
SEO Audit
11 / 16 ON-PAGE CHECKS PASSING

The page meets two of Google's technical minimums: it returns HTTP 200 and is indexable, with no noindex signal. But it struggles on the third: indexable content. Rendered word count is only 6, there is no visible H1, no links, and no meaningful body text for Google to understand beyond the title and meta description. Metadata quality is good, but the page is too thin to satisfy people-first content expectations.

SEO ISSUES
og:image needs attention
INFO

og:image is 1024x576px — below the recommended 1200x630 for large summary cards.

Fix: Serve a reachable og:image at 1200x630 (600x315 minimum for non-large cards) and keep it under ~1MB for fast social unfurls.
No robots.txt found
INFO

A robots.txt was not found at the site root. Crawlers cannot discover crawl rules or a sitemap reference.

Fix: Add a /robots.txt that allows crawling of public pages and includes a `Sitemap:` line pointing to your sitemap.xml.
No valid sitemap.xml found
INFO

A valid XML sitemap was not found at /sitemap.xml. Sitemaps help search engines discover and prioritize your pages.

Fix: Generate a sitemap.xml (a `<urlset>` of your public URLs) and reference it from robots.txt.
Address mismatch (NAP inconsistency)
WARNING

The postal address in structured data does not appear in the visible page text. Consistent name/address/phone is a key local-SEO signal.

Fix: Ensure the structured-data PostalAddress matches the address displayed on the page and across directory listings.
Physical address without LocalBusiness schema
INFO

The page shows a physical address but has no LocalBusiness (or subtype) JSON-LD, so search engines cannot reliably associate the location with the business.

Fix: Add LocalBusiness JSON-LD with name, address, telephone, geo, and openingHours to strengthen local-SEO eligibility.
Add meaningful indexable body content
CRITICAL

Google can index the page, but there is almost nothing to index: rendered word count is 6 and the visible text is effectively empty. This is a direct technical-requirement problem because the page lacks meaningful indexable content.

Fix: Publish visible HTML content on the page: an H1, short intro, project summaries, skills, education, and contact details. Make sure the first screen contains real text that matches the title "AI/ML Engineering Student".
Add a visible H1 that matches the page topic
WARNING

The page has h1Count=0 despite a clear topic in the title. Without a visible main heading, both users and search engines get a weaker page-level signal about what the content is about.

Fix: Add one visible H1 such as "Tushar Kapoor, AI/ML Engineering Student" at the top of the main content. Keep it aligned with the existing title and introductory copy.
Add internal and external links to support discovery
WARNING

The page has 0 internal links and 0 external links. That leaves Google with no on-page pathways to related content such as project pages, GitHub repositories, LinkedIn, or a resume.

Fix: Add links to project detail pages or anchored sections, plus external links to GitHub, LinkedIn, and a PDF resume. Use descriptive anchor text like "View fraud detection project" instead of generic labels.
Create robots.txt and sitemap.xml
WARNING

robots.txt is missing (404) and there is no sitemap.xml. These are not required for ranking, but for a small portfolio they are easy wins for crawl clarity and discovery.

Fix: Publish /robots.txt with a Sitemap line pointing to /sitemap.xml, then create a valid sitemap listing the homepage and any project subpages. Submit the sitemap in Google Search Console.
Add a Twitter card for richer social previews
INFO

Open Graph tags are present, but twitterCard.present is false. This does not affect Google rankings, yet it weakens presentation when the page is shared on X and similar clients.

Fix: Add a twitter:card tag, ideally summary_large_image if you also upgrade the share image dimensions. Reuse the existing title, description, and image values.
Upgrade the Open Graph image size
INFO

The declared og:image is valid and fetchable, but at 1024x576 it is below the recommended 1200x630 for large summary cards. This is a shareability issue rather than a Google indexing issue.

Fix: Export a 1200x630 social banner and update the og:image reference to that file. Keep text minimal and legible for previews.
SEO OPPORTUNITIES
Turn each project into its own indexable page
HIGH EFFORT

Create separate URLs for major projects instead of keeping everything implicit on the homepage. Each page should target a specific topic cluster such as deep learning project, IoT sensor pipeline, or algorithmic problem solving, with original detail about the problem, approach, stack, and outcomes.

Impact: This creates multiple entry points for long-tail search and gives the site enough substance to rank beyond branded queries.
Write an opening snippet-worthy introduction
LOW EFFORT

Because Google often generates snippets from visible page text rather than the meta description, the first on-page paragraph should clearly summarize who Tushar Kapoor is, what he builds, and what visitors can find here. Right now there is no visible opening copy for snippet generation.

Impact: Better snippet text can improve click-through for branded and profile-style searches.
Expand structured data beyond Person schema
MEDIUM EFFORT

Keep the Person schema, but add properties such as sameAs links to GitHub/LinkedIn and consider structured data for project subpages where relevant. The current single Person JSON-LD object is a good start, but it does not expose project-level detail.
